Session Cookie Missing Security Flags

Medium
auth_tests

http://127.0.0.1:3001/#/

1

Log in as 'admin@juice-sh.op' (role: admin)

2

Visit http://127.0.0.1:3001/#/ -- the finding is visible in what the page exposes here

cookie 'continueCode': httpOnly=False, secure=False, sameSite='Lax'

What this means

cookie 'continueCode' is missing the HttpOnly flag -- identified as a session/auth cookie because it was newly issued or changed value across the login boundary for role 'admin'.

How to fix it

Set HttpOnly and Secure on every session/auth cookie, and never set SameSite=None without also setting Secure.

Concurrent Session Not Revoked On Re-Login

Medium
auth_tests

http://127.0.0.1:3001/#/

1

Log in as 'admin@juice-sh.op' (role: admin)

2

Visit http://127.0.0.1:3001/#/ -- the finding is visible in what the page exposes here

HTTP 200, 9393 bytes (post-second-login replay)

What this means

The session cookie captured from a first login for role 'admin' still authenticates against 'http://127.0.0.1:3001/#/' (HTTP 200) after a second, independent login for the same role has completed -- the server does not revoke prior sessions when a new one is established.

How to fix it

Either revoke prior sessions when a new authentication event occurs for the same account, or provide the user a way to view and remotely terminate concurrent sessions, per the OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet.

Predictable / Low-Entropy Session Token

Medium
TC-128.5

http://127.0.0.1:3001/#/

1

Log in as 'admin@juice-sh.op' (role: admin)

2

Visit http://127.0.0.1:3001/#/ -- the finding is visible in what the page exposes here

cookie 'token': two independently-issued tokens for this cookie share an identical 542-character prefix, suggesting a predictable/non-random component

What this means

Cookie 'token' -- two independently-issued tokens for this cookie share an identical 542-character prefix, suggesting a predictable/non-random component.

How to fix it

Generate session identifiers with a cryptographically secure PRNG carrying at least 64 bits of entropy, with no fixed, sequential, or otherwise predictable component, per the OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet.

Missing Rate Limiting At The API/Token Level

Medium
TC-129.3

http://127.0.0.1:3001/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=polling&t=Q1dPWJv

This finding's replay couldn't be captured automatically: replay timed out after 20s using the 'no_rate_limit' player. See the technical report for the underlying evidence.

What this means

6 consecutive authenticated requests to 'http://127.0.0.1:3001/socket.io/?EIO=4&transport=polling&t=Q1dPWJv' produced no HTTP 429 or throttling-shaped response -- this API endpoint has no observable rate limiting at the authenticated/token level, beyond whatever login-only limiting TC-129.3 already checks.

How to fix it

Apply per-token/per-account rate limiting to authenticated API endpoints, not just the unauthenticated login endpoint.

Default Configuration -- Missing or Weak Content-Security-Policy

Medium
TC-128.5

http://127.0.0.1:3001

1

Visit http://127.0.0.1:3001 -- the finding is visible in what the page exposes here

Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8 Content-Security-Policy: None

What this means

'http://127.0.0.1:3001' no CSP header present (Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8). This is a defense-in-depth gap, not a confirmed exploit path on its own -- it only matters if the application also has an injection point (e.g. reflected/DOM XSS) for a CSP to have blocked, consistent with real disclosed reports of this class (HackerOne #225833) being low-severity precisely because they lacked an actual XSS to chain with.

How to fix it

Deploy a strict Content-Security-Policy on every HTML response (e.g. script-src 'self' plus nonces/hashes for any required inline scripts) with no unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval/wildcard sources.

Sensitive Content Cacheable After Logout (Back/Refresh Attack)

Low
auth_tests

http://127.0.0.1:3001/#/

1

Log in as 'admin@juice-sh.op' (role: admin)

2

Visit http://127.0.0.1:3001/#/ -- the finding is visible in what the page exposes here

Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8 Cache-Control: public, max-age=0

What this means

'http://127.0.0.1:3001/#/' authenticated response has no Cache-Control: no-store/no-cache directive -- a shared or public browser's back-button/disk cache can replay this authenticated page's content even after the user has logged out.

How to fix it

Set Cache-Control: no-store (and Pragma: no-cache for older HTTP/1.0 caches) on every authenticated response.

Session Not Bound To Client Fingerprint (Hijacking Risk)

Low
auth_tests

http://127.0.0.1:3001/#/

1

Log in as 'admin@juice-sh.op' (role: admin)

2

Visit http://127.0.0.1:3001/#/ -- the finding is visible in what the page exposes here

HTTP 200, 9393 bytes

What this means

The session cookie for role 'admin' is accepted from a client presenting a completely different User-Agent than the one that logged in -- the session is not bound to any client fingerprint, so a stolen cookie alone (no other client secret) is sufficient to hijack the session from a different device/browser.

How to fix it

This is a defense-in-depth gap, not a standalone vulnerability (per-request client-binding is unusual and has real usability tradeoffs) -- consider it alongside session lifetime/rotation controls, not as a required fix on its own.

Default Configuration -- Path-Relative StyleSheet Import

Low
TC-128.1

http://127.0.0.1:3001

1

Visit http://127.0.0.1:3001 -- the finding is visible in what the page exposes here

<link rel=stylesheet> with path-relative href(s): styles.css, styles.css

What this means

'http://127.0.0.1:3001' imports 2 stylesheet(s) using an href relative to the current page's own path rather than the site root: styles.css, styles.css. If this page can ever be rendered at an unexpected/attacker-influenced path (a path-based router, a reflected-path error page), the browser resolves that relative href against the wrong base and can be made to load an attacker-controlled stylesheet from a trusted origin -- a known technique for exfiltrating page content via CSS selectors/attribute readers.

How to fix it

Reference stylesheets with a root-relative ('/css/app.css') or absolute (https://...) href, never one relative to the current page's own path.
